title: How I used A.I to finish a 7-year journey
author: AlienBloomPoker
selftext:
How it started:   
7 years ago I was playing with cards in a poker room and decided I want to play RISK. 24 hours later I had the initial world map design and have been adding/refining all kinds of new mechanics into it over the years using just a deck of cards.

Enter ChatGPT 2025:   
I never used A.I before December 2025. But after messing around with it in Unity, I felt confident I could finally bring my game to the world. After spending 8 hours a day with my butt glued to my chair for 8 months, I finally did it. I finally had the first working version of Alien Bloom online for everyone to play.

And it bombed. Hard.

The biggest hurdles were game-breaking bugs I never encountered when I playtest for hours and players had no idea what was going on or how to play.  
  
How its going:  
I've since fixed a lot of the bugs, added in a tutorial, banners and info buttons to help Players; But in the end, building a unique, great game wasn't enough...and I'm not really sure which direction to take anymore. Gaming seems to be dying. In trying to promote my game, I've read some of the most hateful comments including; "Your spaceship looks like a penis ha ha! I'm glad you excluded New Zealand from your game, because the game is shit." I had a Twitch streamer test out the game and at the time I was testing AI art for the steam capsule only, one of his mods left out of protest because if I put that much effort into my capsule, then the rest of the game must be shit (despite it having no AI art outside of that limited test).  
  
Pretty demoralizing. I made a great game and now its like I built an aircraft carrier in a [lake.lol](http://lake.lol)  
  
A.I Work Process:  
I used to stick to the ChatGPT website and copy/paste individual scripts form there, not realizing Codex existed or how best to use it. Now I use the ChatGPT chats like an agent, explain what I want and they prepare a prompt for Codex to use and implement. So far its been working really well on 6.0 Sol with usually only 1 more clean up prompt needed after a new implementation.   
  
Going Forward:  
Alien Bloom is my baby. I'm not ready to give up on her for at least another year and I'll keep adding new game modes in hopes that it gets picked up one day by players.
